projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Rosalie J. Hughes was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: [transcript was created in all capital letters] WE'RE AMERICANS REMEMBERED, INTERVIEWING ROSALIE J. HUGHES, ON JUNE 30TH, 2003 AT HER HOME IN MERRIAM, KANSAS. SHE WAS BORN ON THE 12TH OF DECEMBER, 1922, AND WORKED IN A B-25 BOMBER PLANT MAKING B-25 BOMBERS IN KANSAS CITY, KANSAS, AT THE FAIRFAX BOMBER PLANT FROM AUGUST 13TH, 1942, TO APRIL 19TH, 1945. SHE WAS A RIVETER. THIS IS ROSIE THE RIVETER. ROSIE, WHERE DID YOU GROW UP AS A YOUNG GIRL?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: KANSAS CITY, KANSAS, UP ON ARGENTINE.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: IN ARGENTINE, KANSAS?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I'VE LIVED IN THREE HOUSES.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: THREE HOUSES?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: GONE TO THREE SCHOOLS.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: MOM, DAD, BUNCH OF KIDS?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: MY MOTHER, MY FATHER, I HAD THREE BIG BROTHERS.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: THREE BIG BROTHERS?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: AND MY BIG BROTHERS WERE WELL-KNOWN. ONE BROTHER, RAY MCDONALD, WAS A BOXING CHAMPION, AND THREE BIG BROTHERS. I, AS THE DAUGHTER, WAS THE RUNT. THEY CALLED ME "RUNT."

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: YEAH, YOU WERE THE BABY, BUT OF COURSE, THE FAVORITE ONE IN THE FAMILY BECAUSE YOU WERE A GIRL AND YOU HAD THREE BIG BROTHERS. WHAT DID YOUR DADDY DO FOR A LIVING?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: MY DADDY WAS A SWITCH ENGINEER FOR THE SANTA FE RAILROAD.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: IN THE ARGENTINE YARDS, I BET?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: IN THE ARGENTINE YARDS.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: NOW THAT IS GOOD. SO JUST KIND OF A NORMAL HOME LIFE GROWING UP?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: MY DADDY WAS FROM SCOTLAND.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: HE WAS NOT BORN IN THE UNITED STATES?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: NO. MY DADDY WAS BORN IN SCOTLAND. GLASGOW, SCOTLAND HE CAME OVER HERE -- HIS UNCLE SENT FOR HIM TO COME OVER TO HELP HIM ON THE FARM -- IN OKLAHOMA. MY DADDY DIDN'T LIKE LIVING ON THAT FARM IN OKLAHOMA, AND HE HAD HEARD ABOUT THE RAILROAD, SO HE LEFT THE FARM IN OKLAHOMA, IN EDMOND OKLAHOMA, AND CAME UP TO ATCHISON AND GOT WORKING FOR THE SANTA FE RAILROAD.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: YOUR MOTHER WAS BORN IN THE UNITED STATES?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: MY MOTHER WAS BORN IN NAPOLEON, MISSOURI.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: OKAY, SO THEY GOT MARRIED AND HAD FOUR CHILDREN; THREE BOYS AND A GIRL, CORRECT?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: YES. ALL BORN AT 1825 SOUTH VALLEY.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: 1825 SOUTH VALLEY, IN KANSAS CITY, KANSAS. ANY OF YOUR BROTHERS SERVE IN THE MILITARY?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: MY BROTHER BILL WAS AN ENGINEER IN THE STEEL PLANT. BUT HE WAS A 4-F. EVERYBODY WANTED TO KNOW HOW COME THAT GREAT BIG, STRONG BROTHER ISN'T IN THE AIR FORCE -- I MEAN ISN'T IN THE SERVICE -- HE WAS 4-F. BUT MY BROTHER RAY, MY BROTHER RAY MCDONALD, WAS IN THE NAVY AND SERVED IN ENGLAND AND EVEN OVER THERE IN EUROPE ABOUT THE SAME TIME JERRY WAS, MY HUSBAND WAS. THEY COULD HAVE BEEN IN THE SAME HOSPITAL AT THE SAME TIME.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: HOW ABOUT YOUR OTHER BROTHER?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: AND MY BROTHER CHARLES, HE WAS A RIFLEMAN AND HE WAS WITH THE, HE WENT IN, HE WAS ALREADY IN THE NATIONAL GUARD IN 1941, ER, 1939, 1941 HE TOLD US THAT THEY WERE MOBILIZING THE NATIONAL GUARD AND THEN HE WAS SENT TO SAN FRANCISCO. HE WAS IN THE ARMY, BUT THE WAR BROKE OUT ON DECEMBER 7TH AND THEY WENT ONTO THE INVASION OF GUADALCANAL AS A MARINE. THE ARMY WENT IN AS MARINES.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: DOES HE RETURN HOME SAFELY?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: YES, YES. HE WAS IN THE BATTLE OF GUADALCANAL AND THE BATTLE OF BOUGAINVILLE. HE WAS LOST IN THE JUNGLE AND THEY FOUND HIM. HE HAD MALARIA AND HE DOESN'T REMEMBER THAT AT ALL. THEN WE WERE INFORMED HE WAS LOST. WE WERE NEVER INFORMED HE WAS MISSING AND MY MOTHER SAID, I KNOW HE'S ALIVE, I KNOW CHARLES IS ALIVE. AND MY BROTHER RAY WAS IN THE HOSPITAL AT THAT TIME IN ENGLAND. HE WAS HURT ON THE SHIP WITH A STORM AT SEA -- NEITHER ONE OF MY BROTHERS GOT PURPLE HEARTS OR ANYTHING -- BUT MY MOTHER HAD ONE SON IN THE HOSPITAL IN ENGLAND, AND WE DIDN'T KNOW WHERE CHARLES WAS BUT MY MOM KNEW HE WAS ALIVE. IN THE MEANTIME, MY MOTHER WORKED AS A GRAY LADY, AS A RED CROSS GRAY LADY, DOING WHAT SHE COULD FOR THE WAR, TAKING BLOOD, AND MY DAD WAS AN AIR-RAID WARDEN. HE DID ALL HE COULD FOR THE WAR. ALL I COULD DO -- I WASN'T GOING TO THE SERVICE -- MY MOTHER SAID IF YOU WANT TO DO SOMETHING FOR THE WAR, THEY'RE GOING TO BUILD AIRPLANES DOWN THERE, GO DOWN THERE. SO THAT'S WHAT I DID. I GAVE UP COLLEGE.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: OKAY, YOU'D GRADUATED FROM HIGH SCHOOL, AND THEN YOU WENT TO JUNIOR COLLEGE A YEAR OR SO, AND YOU COULD HAVE KEPT ON GOING, BUT YOU WANTED TO HELP IN THE WAR EFFORT SO YOU WENT DOWN TO THE BOMBER PLANT IN FAIRFAX?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I TRADED HAD MY SCHOOL BOOKS FOR A TOOLBOX, AND THAT'S ANOTHER STORY -- THE TOOL BOX.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: WELL, WHY DON'T YOU TELL US THAT STORY?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: WELL I DIDN'T KNOW A HAMMER FROM ANYTHING ELSE. I WAS A COLLEGE GIRL IN A SORORITY. AN ENTIRELY DIFFERENT LIFE.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: SO, WHEN DID YOU START AT THE BOMBER PLANT?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: AFTER I GOT TRAINED THEY GAVE US A LIST OF WHAT WE HAD TO HAVE. ONE WAS A TOOL BOX WITH DIFFERENT TOOLS LIKES PLIERS, SCREWDRIVERS AND YOU HAD TO HAVE A WHOLE LOT OF THESE DIFFERENT THINGS. SO I TOOK IT HOME AND I SHOWED MY DAD THAT I HAD TO HAVE A TOOL BOX. WELL, HE COULDN'T TAKE TIME OFF TO TAKE ME UP TO BUY A TOOL BOX, SO BEING SCOTTISH, MY DADDY'S SCOTTISH, HE GAVE ME SOME MONEY TO GO UP TO MONTGOMERY WARDS -- I HAD TO GO TO MONTGOMERY WARDS -- AND BUY A TOOL BOX.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: UP ON KANSAS AVENUE, THAT ONE?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: NO, MINNESOTA AVENUE. SO, I WENT UP WITH MY MOTHER, AND MY BROTHER TOOK ME UP TO GET MY TOOL BOX AND. I SAW THESE THINGS, THESE TOOL BOXES, AND THEY WANTED TOO MUCH MONEY. I HAD ONLY SO MUCH MONEY TO SPEND AND, BEING SCOTTISH, I WASN'T GOING TO SPEND ALL THAT MONEY THAT MY DAD GAVE ME. SO, I LOOK AT THESE BOXES AND I PICKED ONE UP THAT I FIGURED WAS A TOOL BOX, AND THEN I BOUGHT PLIERS AND ALL THOSE THINGS THAT I DIDN'T KNOW WHAT THEY WERE FOR AND ANYWAY, THEY WENT IN MY TOOL BOX. AND THEN, WHEN MY DADDY SAW THESE THE NEXT DAY HE SAYS, "WHAT IS THAT?", AND I SAID, "THAT IS MY TOOL BOX," AND HE SAID, "THAT IS NOT A TOOL BOX, IT'S A FISHING TACKLE BOX."

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: {LAUGHING} HA HA.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: BUT I CARRIED MY FISHING TACKLE BOX WITH ALL MY TOOLS, MY DRILL MOTOR, AND EVERYTHING IN THAT FISHING TACKLE BOX.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: SO YOU, DID YOU RIDE THE BUS TO GET TO THE --

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: 0H, TO GET OVER THERE? SOMETIMES I HAD A RIDE. WE RODE IN RIDES, BUT ON MY DAY OFF OR ON MY DRIVERS DAY OFF, I WOULD HAVE TO GO DOWN TWO HILLS TO GET TO THE BUS ON RIVEE AVENUE AND THEN TRANSFER 7TH STREET TO THE FAIRFAX AND THAT'S HOW I GOT AROUND. AND THEN, IF I DIDN'T HAVE A RIDE, I WOULD HAVE TO GET ON THE BUS TO FAIRFAX GO OVER TO 12TH AND MAIN --

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: -- IN KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI? FROM KANSAS CITY, KANSAS AND THEN GET ON A BUS?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: GO TO 7TH STREET AND KANSAS AVENUE AND TRANSFER TO THE ARGENTINE BUS WHERE I GOT OFF ON SOUTH VALLEY, STAYED ON THE HILL, THEN WALK UP TWO HILLS TO GET TO MY JOB.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: WHAT TIME DID YOU HAVE TO GO TO WORK IN THE MORNING.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: OH, I WOULD GET UP AT, WE HAD TO BE AT WORK AT SEVEN.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: SO, YOU PROBABLY HAD TO GET UP BEFORE FIVE BECAUSE OF THE LONG BUS RIDE AND TRANSFERRING ON THE BUS?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: MOST OF THE TIME I HAD A RIDE, WE HAD SHARED OUR RIDES, BUT WHEN I DIDN'T I HAD TO FIND -- THERE WAS ONE WOMAN WHO LIVED ON ROSEDALE, SO ON MY DRIVER'S DAY OFF, TO GET TO WORK I WOULD HAVE TO GO DOWN TO HER HOUSE DOWN IN ROSEDALE TO GET A RIDE TO GET TO FAIRFAX. IT WAS ONE TIME OR TWO TIMES. IT WAS REAL SNOWY. I HAD TO WALK IN THE DARK OF THE NIGHT OR EARLY MORNING. I HAD A GO DOWN TO DAVIS AVENUE AND 10TH STREET AND ON DOWN TO ROSEDALE TO GET A RIDE TO GO TO FAIRFAX.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: DO YOU RECALL WHAT YOUR WAGE WAS WHEN YOU STARTED OUT, HOW MUCH AN HOUR?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I SAW ONE OF MY PAYCHECKS THE OTHER DAY AND IT LOOKED LIKE IT SAID THIRTY FIVE CENTS AN HOUR.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: THIRTY FIVE CENTS AN HOUR, HUH? IT PROBABLY COST YOU A NICKEL ON THE BUS OR A DIME. OKAY SO, WHAT WAS YOUR FIRST DAY THERE?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: MY FIRST DAY, THEY PUT ME TO WORK ON THE BOMBARDIER. I STARTED WITH THE BOMBARDIER. WE BUILT THAT BOMB'S NOSE FROM SCRATCH. WE BUILT A TUB THAT IS WHERE I DID MY RIVETING ON THE TUB. THAT'S THE GLASS PART, THE PLEXIGLASS PART, ON THE BOMBARDIER'S NOSE. WHERE IS ONE OF MY AIRPLANES? {LOOKS AROUND FOR A MODEL OF A BOMBARDIER AIRPLANE.} THE NOSE HUB. THAT IS WHAT WE RIVETED. {POINTING.} WE SLAPPED THESE PIECES, THE ALUMINUM, AND RIVETED THOSE PIECES, THE ALUMINUM, TOGETHER AND IT MADE A TUB. WE ALSO MADE A PLEXIGLASS NOSE. I DIDN'T DO TOO MUCH ON THAT, WE HAD A LADY NAMED MINNIE, SHE COULD SAW THOSE PIECES ON THE PLEXIGLASS. SHE WAS SO GOOD. AND THEN WE'D PUT THEM UP. I'D HELP THEM PUT THE PLEXIGLASS WINDOWS TOGETHER. BUT MY FIRST JOB WAS GOING OUT ON THE AIRPORT OUT THERE ON THE RAMP AND HOLD A HOSE. THE FIRST DAY OF WORK, HOLD A HOSE OVER THIS NOSE TO SEE IF IT WAS LEAKING.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: AFTER YOU'D RIVETED AND PUT IT TOGETHER?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: NO, NO. MY FIRST DAY OF WORK -- I DIDN'T -- THIS WAS MY FIRST DAY, I HAD TO GO OUT AND CHECK THE NOSE.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: THAT OTHERS HAD DONE.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: AND HOLD A HOSE TO SEE.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: WELL, AT THIRTY FIVE CENTS AN HOUR, WHAT DO YOU EXPECT?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: THAT WAS MY FIRST JOB. THEN I WENT BACK AND THEY STARTED ME ON THE RIVETING, AND THAT IS WHAT I DID UNTIL FISHER BODY -- NOW I DON'T KNOW WHAT YEAR THAT WAS -- THAT FISHER BODY QUIT BUILDING CARS AND THEY STARTED WITH THESE PARTS AND THINGS. FISHER BODY BUILT THESE PARTS AND THEY ALSO BUILT THIS PILOT'S COMPARTMENT. SO THAT IS WHEN I WAS PROMOTED ON UP THE LINE AND BECAME THE MECHANIC.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: SO THEY SENT YOU TO MECHANIC SCHOOL?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: WELL, I WAS ALREADY A MECHANIC. I WAS TRAINED TO BE A MECHANIC.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: BEFORE YOU STARTED?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: WE WERE TAUGHT RIVETING AND WE WERE TAUGHT MECHANICS, HOW TO LAYOUT AND DRILL, HOW TO LAYOUT AND DRILL, AND RIVET AND THEN I WAS TAUGHT HOW TO BE AN ELECTRICIAN. I WAS TAUGHT ALL THESE THINGS BEFORE I GRADUATED FROM THE SCHOOL, THE CIVIL DEFENSE SCHOOL.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: AND IF YOU HADN'T GRADUATED FROM THE CIVIL DEFENSE SCHOOL, YOU WOULDN'T HAVE HAD THE JOB. THEY WANTED TO MAKE SURE YOU COULD DO WHAT YOU WERE ASKED TO DO.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: THAT'S RIGHT. IT'S ENTIRELY DIFFERENT THAN BEING A COLLEGE GIRL.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: I'M SURE OF THAT. NOW, DO YOU HAVE ANY IDEA, HOW MANY OF THEM DID YOU WORK ON A DAY OR DOES IT TAKE SEVERAL DAYS JUST TO DO ONE NOSE?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: WHEN I FIRST WENT TO WORK WE HAD, WITH ONE GIRL BUCKING AND MY RIVETING THIS, WE PUT OUT TWO, MAYBE, A DAY, AND THEN WITH MINNIE AND THEM ON THE NOSE, ON THE PLEXIGLASS PART OF THE NOSE WHICH IS SO IMPORTANT, WE PROBABLY PUT OUT -- I'M HAVING TO GUESS -- WE PUT OUT AT LEAST THREE A DAY. BUT THEN, WHEN FISHER BODY TOOK OVER THE NUMBERS STARTED GOING UP. WE STARTED PUTTING OUT MORE AIRPLANES.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: DO YOU HAVE ANY IDEA HOW MANY AIRPLANES A DAY CAME OFF THE ASSEMBLY LINE?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: AT THAT TIME WHEN I FIRST WENT TO WORK?

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: OR ANY TIME THAT YOU WERE THERE WORKING?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: OH, IT INCREASED.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: OKAY, AT THE HIGH POINT, THOUGH, DO YOU HAVE ANY IDEA HOW MANY BOMBERS YOU WERE PUTTING OUT A DAY? TEN, TWENTY, THIRTY?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I WAS RIGHT UP THERE IN THE FRONT OF THE ASSEMBLY, AND I HAVE TO SAY IT COULD BE -- NO -- I COULDN'T TELL YOU FOR SURE HOW MANY.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: SO YOU STARTED OUT, THEN YOU BECAME A RIVETER AND THEN AS THEY KNEW WHO YOU WERE AND THEY KNEW THE KIND OF WORK YOU COULD DO -- YOU WERE ALREADY CERTIFIED AS A MECHANIC BECAUSE YOU HAD TO DO THAT TO PASS THE SCHOOL TO GET THE JOB -- SO YOU BECAME A MECHANIC AND WHAT DID YOU DO THEN?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: THEY PUT ME ON UP THE LINE, BECAUSE FISHER BODY WAS DOING THIS AND I BECAME AN INSTALLER AND I INSTALLED ALL OF THE THINGS ON THE INSIDE. AT THAT TIME, ALL OF THE THINGS ON THE INSIDE, LIKE THE HEATER, AND THE WIRES, THE OXYGEN LINES, THE GAS LINES, AND ALL THAT SORT OF STUFF, I PUT IN, IN THE NOSE. I DIDN'T HAVE ANYTHING TO DO WITH PUTTING THAT PART ON THE NOSE. I DID ALL THE INSTALLATION ON THE HEATERS, AND ALL THAT WIRING AND STUFF.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: WAS THAT EARLIER IN THE ASSEMBLY LINE PROCESS?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I WORKED A GOOD YEAR RIVETING, SO THEN IN 1943, OR '42, I DON'T KNOW WHEN FISHER BODY STARTED THAT, BUT THAT IS WHEN I STARTED THAT. THEN, I WORKED INSIDE ALL OF THESE FOR QUITE A WHILE, AND THEN I WAS SENT ON UP FURTHER WHERE I WORKED IN THE PILOT'S COMPARTMENT -- THIS ONE HERE -- AND I DID INSTALLATION FROM THE PILOT'S COMPARTMENT AND THROUGH TO THE BOMBARDIER'S COMPARTMENT. THEY WERE CALLED THE ENCLOSURES.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: IF YOU WERE TO GUESS HOW MANY PEOPLE WERE WORKING ON THAT AT THE SAME TIME, HOW MANY DID THEY HAVE ON ENCLOSURES AT THE SAME TIME? TWENTY, 40, 60.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: THE PILOT'S COMPARTMENT WAS SEPARATED ON THE SAME NOSE -- WE WERE ALL IN DEPARTMENT 26, BUT THE PILOT'S COMPARTMENT AND THE NOSE COMPARTMENT WERE SEPARATED THEN. THEN, THEY PUT THEM TOGETHER AND THEN I WAS TRANSFERRED. I DIDN'T WORK IN THE PILOT'S COMPARTMENT. THERE WAS A HATCH UP HERE AS I PUT IN THE SHADES, THE LIGHTS, THE SHADES THAT KEPT THE SUN OUT OF THE PILOT'S FACE. I PUT IN ALL OF THE WIRING. I PULLED THE WIRING UP FROM THE FUSELAGE. WE HAD TO HAVE WIRING IN THE PART FOR THE PILOT AND THE CO-PILOT. AND THEN THERE WAS A BOMB RELEASE DOWN HERE. AND THEN I DID WIRING FOR ALL THE OXYGEN AND ALL THAT, JUST LIKE I DID WITH THIS, MAP CASES, CIGARETTE THINGS, ALL OF THOSE THINGS THAT THEY HAD TO HAVE IN THE PILOT'S COMPARTMENT. WHAT I THINK IS INTERESTING, WE PUT IN AIRPLANES FOR THE UNITED STATES, CHINA AND GREAT BRITAIN. AND I DID THE INSTALLATION OF ALL THESE THINGS THAT THEY HAD TO HAVE TO MAKE THINGS MORE COMFORTABLE FOR THEM. THE ONES THAT WENT TO RUSSIA GOT EVERYTHING, THE ONES THAT WENT TO GREAT BRITAIN GOT JUST ABOUT EVERYTHING, BUT THE ONES THAT WENT TO CHINA DIDN'T HAVE HARDLY ANYTHING. SO I HAD TO ASK, JUST HOW COME CHINA DOESN'T GET ALL OF THESE THINGS AND HE WOULD ANSWER MY QUESTIONS, "YOURS IS NOT TO REASON WHY, YOURS IS BUT TO DO." MY BOSS WOULD SAY THAT. SO, I THOUGHT THAT WAS ALWAYS INTERESTING. THEN THIS HERE PART WAS PUT ON, AS PROGRESS WENT, AND MORE AIRPLANES WENT ON, WE WERE PUT ON A CONVEYER LINE SO I WAS SENT OVER ACROSS TO ANOTHER DEPARTMENT, BUT I KEPT MY BADGE NUMBER, I KEPT MY DEPARTMENT NUMBER, AND I WORKED ON UPSTAIRS ON THE LINE WITH THIS PART OF THE AIRPLANE, THAT FRONT PART. I NEVER WORKED ANYPLACE BUT THE PILOT AND THE BOMBARDIER. AND I HAD MY STATION AND I HAD TO HAVE MY WORK DONE BY THE TIME I GOT TO THE NEXT STATION.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: DID YOU WORK THE DAY SHIFT.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I WORKED THE DAY SHIFT.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: THEY PROBABLY HAD PEOPLE WORKING TWENTY-FOUR HOURS?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: OH, YES. I'D GET MAD AT THE NIGHT SHIFT. THEY BROKE INTO MY FISHING TACKLE BOX AND STOLE MY DRILL MOTOR, AND THAT'S ANOTHER STORY, WOULD YOU LIKE TO HEAR THAT? WELL, AFTER I WAS MARRIED AND WE WERE LIVING IN OUR FIRST LITTLE HOUSE, JERRY WANTED TO BORROW THE NEIGHBOR'S DRILL MOTOR AND I MARKED EVERYTHING I HAD WITH AN RN IN MORSE CODE -- EVERYTHING -- AND HERE WAS MY DRILL MOTOR THAT JERRY BORROWED FROM MY NEIGHBOR ACROSS THE STREET.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: HMM, SO HOW LONG DID YOU WORK AT THE BOMBER PLANT? LET'S SEE, JERRY CAME HOME ON LEAVE AND YOU GOT MARRIED?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: WE WERE MARRIED 1944, THE LAST OF 1944. I WORKED AT THE BOMBER PLANT FROM --

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: AUGUST 14TH, 1942, TO APRIL, 1945.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: OCTOBER OF '45. YEAH, BUT I WAS MARRIED IN OCTOBER, YEAH {INAUDIBLE} UNTIL OCTOBER, '44 AND THEN --

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: YOU WORKED FROM OCTOBER TO APRIL AND YOU LEFT ON MATERNITY LEAVE. WERE MOST OF THE PEOPLE DOING THE WORK IN THE BOMBER PLANT ON THE WHOLE, FROM THE FRONT TO THE BACK, FROM THE TAIL TO THE BOMBARDIER'S CABIN, WERE THEY MOSTLY WOMEN?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: OH, NO. THAT WAS INTERESTING TOO, BECAUSE I LIKE PEOPLE, A LOT OF DIFFERENT KINDS OF PEOPLE, ALL NICE. YOU MEET THE NICEST PEOPLE AND I MET VERY GOOD FRIENDS, BUT THEY'RE ALL DIFFERENT SOCIAL FROM KINGS TO THE COMMON MAN. THAT IS WHAT I WORKED WITH.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: DID YOU HAVE MANY MEETINGS, DID YOU HAVE A LOT OF SLOGANS AROUND AT ALL? DID YOU HAVE PEOPLE CONSTANTLY TALKING ABOUT PATRIOTISM AND WHAT YOU WERE DOING FOR THE BOYS OVERSEAS?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I CAN'T REMEMBER, THAT I CAN'T REMEMBER. WE WERE WORKING TO BUILD THE BOMBERS. I WAS A KID AND WE'D GET IN THE PILOT'S COMPARTMENT, THE PILOTS SEAT, AND PRETEND WE WERE BOMBING THE JAPS. BUT THE PATRIOTISM THAT I CAN REMEMBER IS WHEN THE BOMBS -- I WORKED ON THE END OF THE AISLE -- AND THE BOMBS WOULD GO DOWN, THEY WOULD GO BY ME AND THEY WOULD HAVE MESSAGES ON THEM: "THIS IS FOR ED", OR "THIS IS FOR SOMEBODY ELSE." ALL THESE MESSAGES ON THOSE BOMBS I WILL SAY. ANOTHER THING WE DID, MY HUSBAND TALKED ABOUT THE BOMB DRIVE. WE WOULD TAKE DOLLAR BILLS, ALL OF US, WE'D TAKE DOLLAR BILLS AND PUT THEM ON THE AIRPLANES, AND THE AIRPLANE WENT OUT AND THEY WOULD TAKE THOSE DOLLAR BILLS AND MAKE BOMBS AND THINGS FOR THE WAR.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: SO, EVEN THOUGH IT'S VERY HARD WORK, EVERYBODY'S PROUD OF IT?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: OH, I LOVED IT.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: AND PROUD OF WHAT YOU WERE DOING?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I LIKED ALL THE PEOPLE, ALL THE DIFFERENT CLASSES OF PEOPLE, ALL OF THE DIFFERENT, YES, THEY WERE ALL GOOD PEOPLE AND I LIKED MY WORK. I LIKED DOING MY WORK.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: WHAT WAS THE WORST PART ABOUT THE, ABOUT WORKING THERE, BECAUSE IT WAS VERY HARD WORK. WAS THERE SOMETHING ABOUT IT THAT YOU DIDN'T LIKE ABOUT YOUR WORK?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I DIDN'T LIKE MAYBE GOING TO WORK. I DIDN'T DRIVE A CAR AND I LIVED ON THE TOP OF A HILL.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: SO GETTING TO WORK AND GETTING HOME WAS TOUGH BUT IT WAS GREAT WHILE YOU WERE THERE?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: IT WAS.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: AND YOU ENJOYED DOING IT. DID MOST PEOPLE SHARE THAT FEELING? DID MOST PEOPLE SHARE THE FEELING THAT, I LIKE WHAT I'M DOING BECAUSE I KNOW WHAT I'M DOING IS GOOD FOR OUR COUNTRY?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I'M SURE THEY DID. THERE WAS A WAR GOING ON AND THIS IS WHAT WE WERE DOING. IT WAS ALL I COULD DO. I WOULD HAVE LIKED TO JOIN THE SERVICE -- NOW MY BEST FRIEND, SHE JOINED THE NAVY, TWO OF THE GIRLS WERE ABLE TO GO INTO THE NAVY. ONE BECAME AN OFFICER, ONE MARRIED AN OFFICER, BUT I WASN'T ABLE TO. I NEVER WAS OLD ENOUGH. BUT NO, I CAN'T, I CAN'T THINK OF ANYTHING THAT I DIDN'T LIKE.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: WELL, THAT WAS A GREAT ATTITUDE TO HAVE WHEN YOU WERE WORKING BECAUSE YOU HAD MEN --

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: -- I HAD A GOOD TIME.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: MEN AND WOMEN DEPENDING ON THAT PLANE WORKING RIGHT.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: WE'D SOMETIMES GO TO WORK, GET UP IN THE DARK AND COME HOME IN THE DARK. WORKED 14 HOURS SOMETIMES, GETTING THESE PLANES OUT, BUT YOU'RE YOUNG THEN, YOU'RE YOUNG.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: WELL, I THINK, YEAH. I MEAN, YOU WERE YOUNG, YOU WERE CALLED TO DO IT, AND YOU WERE GLAD TO DO IT. AND YOU WERE PHYSICALLY ABLE TO DO IT. YOU JUST DIDN'T LIKE THE COMMUTE TO WORK. IT WASN'T LIKE HOPPING IN THE CAR. IF YOU COULD HAVE HOPPED IN YOUR CAR, YOU'D HAVE BEEN DOWN THERE IN FIFTEEN MINUTES FROM WHERE YOU LIVED, BUT RIDING A BUS -- PARTICULARLY COMING HOME -- CLEAR ACROSS THE BRIDGE ACROSS THE MISSOURI RIVER TO KANSAS CITY MISSOURI AND CATCH ANOTHER BUS BACK, IT WASN'T EASY.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: AND I REALLY DIDN'T MIND THAT.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: MOST PEOPLE DID IT THAT WAY. YOU DID WHAT YOU HAD TO DO. IT WASN'T THE YEAR 2003, IT WAS BACK IN THE '40'S OF 1900. WELL, SO, YOU LEFT IN APRIL OF 1945 AND THAT WAS BECAUSE YOU WERE PREGNANT.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: AND MY BABY WAS BORN IN JULY.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: THE BABY WAS BORN IN JULY, YOUR OLDEST SON, GARY. JERRY, YOU AND HE HAD MARRIED THE YEAR BEFORE WHEN HE CAME HOME. THEN, YOU GOT OUT IN '45. WERE YOU ABLE TO SPEND ANY MORE TIME WITH HIM? WELL, HE WAS GONE BY THEN ALREADY, WASN'T HE?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: YES. BUT MY BROTHER SHOWED UP -- MY BROTHER THAT WAS MISSING. I LIVED AT HOME WITH MY PARENTS. THAT IS QUITE A DIFFERENT LIFE THAN BEING SINGLE, BEING MARRIED. MY PARENTS WERE VERY GOOD, AS I SAY WE WERE SCOTTISH PEOPLE AND BECAUSE MY FATHER WAS FROM SCOTLAND, WE WERE RAISED WITH THE SCOTTISH TRADITIONS. BUT MY BROTHER -- I REMEMBER THE NIGHT MY MOTHER WOKE ME UP AND SAID, ROSALIE, THE RED CROSS JUST CALLED ME AND SAID THAT THEY FOUND CHARLES, MY BROTHER THAT HAD BEEN LOST. GUADALCANAL HAD BEEN WON AND THE SOLDIERS FOUND HIM OVER THERE SO, MY BROTHER THEN CAME HOME AND HE LIVED AT HOME TOO. HE HAD TO BE IN THE ARMY. HE CAME HOME SO I HAD MY BROTHER AND I TO CHUM AROUND WITH AND DO THINGS. I WASN'T JUST STUCK AT HOME.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: I BET THERE WASN'T MUCH SLEEP THE NIGHT YOU FOUND OUT YOUR BROTHER HAD BEEN FOUND?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: YES, YES. WE WERE SO GLAD.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: WHAT A THRILL THAT WAS, I'M SURE. ABSOLUTELY. SO, YOU HAD YOUR BABY IN JULY AND THEN LET'S SEE, JERRY GOT HOME --

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: ON JULY 29TH. HE GOT HOME IN FEBRUARY THE FOLLOWING YEAR.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: SO YOUR CHILD WAS SEVEN MONTHS OLD AND THAT WAS THE FIRST TIME YOU SAW HIM WHEN HE GOT HOME FROM EUROPE?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: AND YOU KNOW, I WAS RAISED, I STAYED AT HOME AND MY PARENTS HAD THAT BABY. AND MY LITTLE BOY HE WOULDN'T GO TO ANY STRANGE MEN. I HAD MY BROTHER THAT CAME HOME FROM THE SOUTH PACIFIC, AND MY DAD, AND MY BIG BROTHER AND NOBODY ELSE. HE WOULDN'T GO TO ANY OTHER STRANGE MAN AND I SAID, OH, WHEN JERRY COMES HOME, WHAT AM I GOING TO DO? HE WENT RIGHT TO HIS DADDY JUST LIKE HE KNEW.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: HE KNEW, IT WAS INSTINCT WASN'T IT?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: THEN WE MOVED TO A LITTLE HOUSE.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: ON VALLEY, WAS IT?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: NO, IT WAS ON TOP OF A HILL.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: STILL IN ARGENTINE THOUGH?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: YES. THAT HOUSE, AND THEN THIS ONE. WE SOLD THAT HOUSE. HE WAS A GOOD CARPENTER AND WE IMPROVED ON THE LITTLE HOUSE THAT WE BOUGHT AND WE SOLD THAT HOUSE AND WE HAVE LIVED HER FOR 50 YEARS.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: FOR 50 YEARS AND YOU'RE ALMOST 59 YEARS MARRIED, YOU AND JERRY, AND TELL ME ONCE AGAIN, I'VE HEARD FROM JERRY. YOU TELL ME ABOUT YOUR CHILDREN AND GRANDCHILDREN.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: WELL, I STAYED HOME. I STAYED HOME BECAUSE MY MOTHER STAYED HOME AND RAISED THE KIDS, AND HE HAD LONG HOURS THAT HE WORKED BEING A SALESMAN, AND I WORKED WITH THE KIDS. I WAS A SUNDAY SCHOOL TEACHER. I WORKED WITH THE CAMPFIRE AND THE BOY SCOUTS -- I WORKED WITH THE SCOUT MOTHERS -- I TAUGHT, I DID BIBLE SCHOOL, I DID ALL I COULD FOR THE KIDS. I'D TAKE THEM TO THEIR BALL TEAMS AND BOWLING, AND ONE DAUGHTER -- SHE'S A NURSE -- I TOOK HER TO TWO DIFFERENT DANCING SCHOOLS, AND I'VE ONE GIRL IN THE AIR FORCE, SHE'S A TOMBOY, AND I HAD TO TAKE HER -- SHE WAS JUST A LITTLE GIRL, IN FIRST GRADE, I THINK -- AND SHE CAME HOME AND SAID SHE WANTED TO PLAY BALL. I SAID SHE WAS TOO LITTLE AND SHE SAID, NO, I'M GOING TO PLAY BALL. SO I TOOK HER OUT TO THE BALL FIELD AND SHE HIT THAT BALL CLEAR ACROSS THE STREET, SO I HAD A BALL PLAYER. AND THEY BECAME SOFT BALL CHAMPIONS AND EVERYTHING. SHE KEPT ON PLAYING VOLLEYBALL, WHEN SHE GRADUATED FROM WICHITA STATE UNIVERSITY, SHE WAS STILL PLAYING SOFTBALL. THEN SHE STARTED PLAYING GOLF. I'D TAKE ONE TO THE BALL GAME, TAKE ANOTHER ONE TO THE BALL GAME, AND TAKE ONE BOWLING. THAT WAS WHAT I DID.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: A STAY AT HOME MOM'S LIFE, YOU BET.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: AND THEN, BUT, DO YOU KNOW, THAT WE LIVE HERE AND WE HAVE THE SAME NEIGHBORS FOR OVER 50 YEARS?

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: THAT IS AMAZING.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: NOT MANY PEOPLE CAN SAY THAT.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: THAT IS WONDERFUL AND SUCH A NICE AREA AND NICE PART OF KANSAS CITY, NICE SECLUDED BLOCK.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: COULDN'T ASK FOR BETTER. WE ARE VERY FORTUNATE. BEN (INAUDIBLE LAST NAME) NEXT DOOR, HE'S A MAN WHO GOES AROUND AS BENJAMIN FRANKLIN.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: IS THAT RIGHT? DO YOU HAVE ANY, MAYBE ANY LAST THOUGHTS ABOUT YOUR JOB, DOING YOUR JOB FOR YOUR COUNTRY AS ROSIE THE RIVETER AT THE B-25 BOMBER PLANT IN FAIRFAX KANSAS DURING WORLD WAR II? ANY LAST COMMENTS ABOUT DOING SOMETHING FOR YOUR COUNTRY?

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I WAS WORKING AND DOING ALL I COULD AND WE WANTED TO GET THAT WAR OVER WITH AND I WAS DOING A LOT OF PRAYING AND I REMEMBER COMING OUT AT THE END OF THE FINAL SUMMER, I WORKED DOWN NEAR THE END OF THE FINAL ASSEMBLY, AND I CAME OUT OF THAT BOMBER PLANT. AND I LOOKED UP AND THERE WAS THE FLAG, OUR FLAG, AND THERE WAS A "V" IN THE CLOUDS. I KNEW THEN THAT WE WERE GOING TO WIN THAT WAR.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: AND WE DID. THANKS TO YOU AND HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF MEN AND WOMEN.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I MET ALL KINDS OF PEOPLE BECAUSE OF WHERE I WORKED AND THE PART WHERE I WORKED, THE FINAL ASSEMBLY. I MET THE PEOPLE FROM BRITAIN, THE PEOPLE FROM CHINA, THE PEOPLE FROM RUSSIA -- THESE PEOPLE WERE THERE BECAUSE THE AIRPLANE BELONGED TO NORTH AMERICAN AVIATION UNTIL IT WENT OUT THE DOOR. AND WHEN IT WENT OUT THE DOOR, THEN THE OTHER COUNTRIES BOUGHT IT. THE UNITED STATES BOUGHT IT, AND CHINA AND ALL, AND I GOT ACQUAINTED WITH ALL OF THOSE DIFFERENT PEOPLE FROM THOSE COUNTRIES.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: WHAT A WONDERFUL EXPERIENCE.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: I DID. I HAD A GOOD EXPERIENCE.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: WELL YOU HAD A GOOD LIFE, AND MAY IT CONTINUE FOR MANY YEARS. ROSALIE, THANKS A LOT.

sp.speaker: Rosalie J. Hughes
sp.p: THANK YOU.

sp.speaker: Gary Swanson
sp.p: YOU'RE WELCOME.
